NATIONAL COMPANY LAW APPELLATE TRIBUNAL
PRINCIPAL BENCH, NEW DELHI
I.A. No. 6679 of 2026 & I.A. No. 6680 of 2026
In
Company Appeal (AT) (Insolvency) No. 1612 of 2026
IN THE MATTER OF:

Navneet Gupta Insolvency Professional
...Appellant
Versus

Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India
...Respondent
Present:

For Appellant
: Mr. Abhishek Anand, Mr. Karan Kohli, Ms. Palak
Kalra and Ms. Shruti Srivastava, Advocates.

Mr. Deepak Khosla, Advocate for the Applicant

For Respondent
: Mr. Naveen Pawah, Sr. Advocate with Mr. Ashish
Verma, Mr. Nikhil Thakur and Ms. Kriti,
Advocates.

Mr. Inderbir Singh Alag, Sr. Advocate with Mr.
Kumar Anurag Singh, Mr. Zain A. Khan, Mr. Dev
Aaryan, Mohd. Abran Khan, Mr. Manoranjan
Nayak and Mr. Nakul Mohta, Advocates.

O R D E R
Per Justice Sharad Kumar Sharma, Member (Judicial)
1.
Before us, under consideration are the two interlocutory applications,
being I.A. Nos. 6680 of 2026 and 6679 of 2026, preferred by Mr. Ajmair
Singh Bhullar and Mr. Haravtar Singh Arora respectively. By virtue of these
applications, the Applicant has sought recall of the Order dated 10.09.2026
that was passed in I.A. No. 6230 of 2026, preferred by the Applicant himself
i.e., Mr. Haravtar Singh Arora, seeking himself to be impleaded in the
proceedings of the Company Appeal, which had already stood rejected.

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
2 of 34
While Mr. Ajmair Singh Bhullar, sought his limited impleadment in stay
application being I.A. No. 6168 of 2026, while he is not party to Company
Appeal.

2.
It becomes indispensable for us to directly consider the application
bearing I.A. No. 6679 of 2026, itself without considering the background and
the manner in which the proceedings have been traversed by the Applicant.

3.
The Company Appeal had been preferred by Mr. Navneet Gupta, the
Insolvency Resolution Professional, wherein the IBBI, the Regulator while
considering the response of Appellant, as submitted in response to the Show
Cause Notice issued to him, for his professional misconduct and dereliction
in discharge of duties as a professional by way of Show Cause Notice (SCN)
No. COMP/11011/110/2025-IBBI/1847/1797 dated 28.11.2025, for taking
Penal action as per the provisions contained in the IBBI (Grievance and
Complaint Handling Procedure) Regulations, 2017, had passed the
impugned Order. Learned IBBI upon establishment of charge against the
Appellant had proceeded to pass the following Order on 21.08.2026 which
has been impugned by the Appellant:

“3.1. The DC in exercise of the powers conferred under
Section 220 of the Code read with Regulation 13 of the
IBBI (Inspection and Investigation) Regulations, 2017
hereby suspends the registration of Mr. Navneet Gupta
(Registration
No.
IBBI/IPA-001/IP-P00361/2017-
18/10619) for a period of one year.

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
3 of 34
3.2. This Order shall come into force on expiry of 30
days from the date of its issue.

3.3. A copy of this order shall be sent to the CoC of all
the corporate debtors in which Mr. Navneet Gupta is
providing his services. The CoC of the respective
corporate debtors shall replace Mr. Navneet Gupta with
another Resolution Professional in terms of Section 27 of
the Code.”

4.
Consequent to the establishment of set of allegations relating to
proportional misconduct the Resolution Professional and the observations
which have been made by the Disciplinary Committee, in exercise of its
statutory powers conferred to it under Section 220 of the Code, which is to
be read with Regulation 13 of the IBBI (Inspection and Investigation)
Regulations, 2017, suspended the registration of Mr. Navneet Gupta, the
IRP (Appellant), for a period of one year.

5.
The Order, in itself, has been directed to be made effective after the
expiry of 30 days from the date of its issuance. What would be more
concerning would be the observations made in Para No. 3.3 of the impugned
Order, which has been argued by the counsel for the parties, whereby the
copy of the Order of suspending the licence of the IRP, was directed to be
sent to the Committee of Creditors (CoC) and to all the Corporate Debtors
(CDs) to which Mr. Navneet Gupta was providing his services as IRP.

6.
Thereafter, it was also directed that the respective CoC of the
Corporate Debtor, shall be placing the Order to the respective CoC of which

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
4 of 34
of Mr. Navneet Gupta was RP for replacing him with another Resolution
Professional in terms of Section 27 of the Code. Section 27 of the Code
prescribes for the replacement of the Resolution Professional by the CoC
upon satisfaction of certain terms and conditions, which has been given in
the Order itself, requiring for conditions for calling for the replacement,
suspension or removal of the Resolution Professional by the CoC. In other
words, the observation made in Para 3.3 of the impugned Order, that would
have only taken effect subject to satisfaction of the conditions contained
under Section 27 of the Code.

7.
At this stage, we are not venturing on the merits of the observations
made in the impugned Order, as extracted above, or its inter se play about
its enforceability under Section 27 of the IBC qua the professional conduct
of Appellant, which is to be decided in the Company Appeal.
8.
One Mr. Haravtar Singh Arora (the Appellant) is shown to have
preferred I.A. No. 6230 of 2026. In the application thus preferred by him on
01.09.2026, Mr. Haravtar Singh Arora prayed that he may be permitted to
be impleaded in the proceedings of the Company Appeal and to permit the
Applicant to exercise his powers under Order I Rule 8A of CPC to participate
in the proceedings in a representative capacity. The relief as modulated by
Mr. Haravtar Singh Arora in, his I.A. No. 6230 of 2026 is extracted
hereunder:-
“That in view of the above facts and circumstances of the
matter, it is humbly prayed that this Hon'ble Appellate
Tribunal may:

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
5 of 34
i. Allow impleadment of the applicant as a Respondent in
the present appeal.

ii. INTERIM RELIEF (1): Permit the applicant the exercise
of his right under Order I (Rule 8A) of the CPC to take such
further part in oral arguments on the questions of law that
arise in these proceedings as may be deemed appropriate
by this Hon'ble Tribunal.

iii.INTERIM RELIEF (2): Permit the power of Attorney
Holder to file a copy of the Power-of-Attorney executed in
favour of Mr. Taman Deep Singh by Mr. Haravtar Singh
Arora, that has already been filed with multiple judicial
forums, including Hon'ble NCLT (Chandigarh), on or before
02-09-2026 before this Hon'ble Appellate Tribunal.

iv. Pass ex parte orders on the above prayers

v. Any further interim order or direction which this Hon'ble
Appellate Tribunal may deem fit and proper in the
circumstances of the case be issued in favour of the
appellant.”

9.
If we see the interim relief, that was sought therein was in context of
the provisions contained under Order I Rule 8A of the CPC, which reads as
under:-
“8A. Power of Court to permit a person or body of
persons to present opinion or to take part in the
proceedings.—While trying a suit, the Court may, if
satisfied that a person or body of persons is
interested in any question of law which is directly
and substantially in issue in the suit and that it is
necessary in the public interest to allow that person

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
6 of 34
or body of persons to present his or its opinion on
that question of law, permit that person or body of
persons to present such opinion and to take such
part in the proceedings of the suit as the Court may
specify.”

10.
Primarily the Applicant wanted to contest the proceedings of Company
Petition in the representative capacity, as provided by Order I Rule 8A of
CPC. This particular nature of contest of proceedings under the I&B Code is
unknown to law, more particularly when the proceedings were against
Resolution Professional, for his misconduct, in these proceedings there
cannot be any such concept of contesting proceedings in a representative
capacity.

11.
Rule 8A of Order I of CPC, was inserted by Act No. 104 of 1976, which
granted the power to the Court to permit a person or a body of persons to
present an opinion or to take part in the proceedings. The provisions of
Order I Rule 8A is not akin to Order I Rule 10 provides for impleadment, it
only contemplate to be attracted when the Court draws an opinion or solicits
to participate, its only when a person or body of persons is “interested in
any question”. Before we venture further, we could see that, upon perusal of
records that the application that was preferred was under a Power of
Attorney, that was executed on 02.09.2026, as prescribed in the note clause
of the application itself. The Power of Attorney in original is on record before
various judicial forums, including NCLT Chandigarh, and it was marked
that copy would be filed with NCLAT by 02.09.2026 positively. We make it

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
7 of 34
clear that till the date of passing of the Order i.e., dated 10.09.2026 which
has been sought to be recalled, this Power of Attorney was never placed on
record of I.A. No. 6230 of 2026 in order to justify the justification of
Vakalatnama of Mr. Haravtar Singh Arora and the authority vested in him
under the Power of Attorney to pursue the proceedings on behalf of the
executant Power of Attorney holder, Mr. Taman Deep Singh. Thus the
application itself was not competent to be considered under is the absence
of valid Power of Attorney being placed on record.

12.
This application, i.e., I.A. No. 6230 of 2026, came up for consideration
before the Co-ordinate Bench of this Tribunal and was decided by an Order
dated 10.09.2026, whereby the application was rejected on the ground that
the Applicant had no right whatsoever to pursue the proceedings either
individually or in representative capacity and the same was accordingly
dismissed. What could be seen from the Order Sheet, that the proceedings
were thereafter taken up on 16.09.2026 and, during the intervening period,
Applicant Mr. Haravtar Singh Arora, filed a recall application on 14.09.2026,
being I.A. No. 6679 of 2026 along with I.A. No. 6680 of 2026, which was
filed by Mr. Ajmair Singh Bhullar wherein: (1) in I.A. No. 6679 of 2026, the
Applicant, Mr. Haravtar Singh Arora, prayed for recalling of the Order dated
10.09.2026 that was passed in I.A. No. 6230 of 2026; (2) In I.A. No. 6680 of
2026, preferred by Mr. Ajmair Singh Bhullar, a prayer was made for to
implead the Applicant, as a limited Respondent only in I.A. No. 6168 of 2026
for grant of interim relief limited for adjudication of prayer No. (iii) & (iv)
thereof.

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
8 of 34

13.
This application for recall of Order 10.09.2026, came up for
consideration before the Co-ordinate Bench and, owing to the fact that the
recall application itself was being pressed upon as if it was an argument
being extended for a regular Appeal, the Co-ordinate Bench declined to hear
the application, and thus it was nominated to us. Monitoring of time to hear
a matter of this nature and that too on a recall is difficult owing to the
expectation of the members of the Bar and at time atrociousness too, which
was exercised by the Applicant. Thus the Co-ordinate Bench, on
17.09.2026, declined to hear because of the fact that the counsel for the
Applicant, persisted hearing the matter on recall application, which was
already argued at length, despite taking note of the fact that there were
other matters pending before the Tribunal which were listed on board.
Hence, the Tribunal was constrained to release the matter, to avoid any
embarrassment in the court proceedings.

14.
When the matter was placed before the Hon’ble Officiating
Chairperson, the Company Appeal has been nominated before us. The
learned counsel for the Applicant, Mr. Deepak Khosla for the Applicant Mr.
Haravtar Singh Arora, has pressed his application I.A. No. 6679 of 2026 and
I.A. No. 6680 of 2026 from the following perspectives: -
a. That a fraud has been played upon the Tribunal,
b. while passing the Order dated 10.09.2026; hence, it deserves to be
recalled.
c. Lack of jurisdiction.

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
9 of 34

15.
We make it very clear that at this point of time itself that when C.A.
(AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026 was being considered with the two IA’s before
the learned Tribunal on 10.09.2026, the learned counsel on behalf of the
Applicant had represented the Applicant with all diligence and perseverance
for which he is known, and was heard to quite an extent on 10.09.2026. It is
at a much belated stage that the Appellant has come with a recall
application by filing the same on 14.09.2026, primarily on the ground (1)
that the order dated 10.09.2026 is actuated by fraud; (2) lack of jurisdiction.

16.
The aspect of fraud has been an oriented venture, argued by the
learned counsel for the Applicant to the recall application, on the ground
that when the reply was filed by the Appellant in objection to I.A. No. 6230
of 2026, the reply was supported by an affidavit, which the Applicant to I.A.
No. 6679 of 2026 contends that, because the affidavit filed in support
thereto was a fraudulent affidavit, it would vitiate the entire proceedings and
thus the reply given by the Appellant, should not have been taken into
consideration by the learned Tribunal while passing the Order dated
10.09.2026, rejecting I.A. No. 1620 of 2026, that was filed by the Applicant,
Mr. Haravtar Singh Arora, under Order I Rule 8A of CPC, for getting himself
impleaded.

17.
We make it very clear at this juncture itself that the ground of fraud,
as articulated now to be argued by the learned counsel for the Applicant,
owing to the affidavit filed in support of reply to I.A. No. 6230 of 2026, is not
pleading anything or any allegation of fraud, with regard to any fraud in the

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
10 of 34
pleading of the application or the reply, but rather had exclusively confined
his arguments upon the affidavit itself and the way it has been sworn. The
counsel for the Applicant to I.A. No. 6679 of 2026, further submits that the
notarized affidavit filed in support of the reply to the impleadment
application, being I.A. No. 6230 of 2026, is not in consonance with Rule 72
of the NCLT Rules, the objection by Applicant was because of the fact that
since the affidavit only speaks about “attestation as identified” and it does
not mention that it was “sworn” on oath. Thus, he submits that contents of
the affidavit in reply could not be taken into consideration for the purposes
of deciding I.A. No. 6230 of 2026 because there was a fraud played by the
Appellant, while filing the reply on 02.09.2026 to I.A. No. 6230 of 2026 filed
for impleadment invoking Order I Rule 8A of CPC.

18.
The counsel for the Applicant submits that much credence cannot be
placed on the contents of para 2 of the affidavit, which explains as to how
the contents have been read and understood by the deponent. In relation
thereto, the learned counsel for the Applicant submitted that because of the
fact that the notarized affidavit dated 02.09.2026 only mentions
“attestation” and it is not a “swearing”, it cannot be treated as an affidavit.

19.
This contention raised by the learned counsel for the Applicant now to
support his recall application is not acceptable by us, and that too when for
the purpose of establishing the so-called theory of fraud as vehemently
argued by the learned counsel for the Appellant is exclusively rather only
based upon the contents of the reply affidavit filed by the Appellant, and

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
11 of 34
more particularly when the contents of the affidavit itself is not denied,
particularly in relation to the pleadings raised therein.

20.
So far as the NCLAT Rules are concerned, the provisions in relation to
the affidavit is contained under Part-XI of the NCLAT Rules. Part-XI reads as
under:-

“67. Title of affidavits.-
Every affidavit shall be titled as “Before the National
Company Law Appellate Tribunal.” followed by the cause
title of the application or other proceeding in which the
affidavit is sought to be used.
68. Form and contents of the affidavit.-
The affidavit as per Form NCLAT-4 shall conform to the
requirements of order XIX, rule 3 of Civil Procedure Code,
1908 (5 of 1908).
69. Persons authorised to attest.-
Affidavits shall be sworn or affirmed before an Advocate
or Notary, who shall affix his official seal.
70. Affidavits of illiterate, visually challenged persons.-
Where an affidavit is sworn or affirmed by any person
who appears to be illiterate, visually challenged or
unacquainted with the language in which the affidavit is
written shall be in Form NCLAT-5, the attestor shall certify
that the affidavit was read, explained or translated by him
or in his presence to the deponent and that he seemed to
understand it, and made his signature or mark in the
presence of the attestor.
71. Identification of deponent.-

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
12 of 34
If the deponent is not known to the attestor, his identity
shall be testified by a person known to him and the person
identifying shall affix his signature in token thereof.
72. Annexures to the affidavit.-
(1) Document accompanying an affidavit shall be referred
to therein as Annexure number and the attestor shall make
the endorsement thereon that this is the document marked
putting the Annexure number in the affidavit.
(2) The attestor shall sign therein and shall mention the
name and his designation.”

21.
The learned counsel for the Applicant had restricted his argument
from the perspective of Rule 72 of the NCLAT Rules, contending thereof that
the affidavit filed in support of the reply/objection, to I.A. No. 6230 of 2026
cannot be read for the purposes of deciding I.A. No. 6230 of 2026 preferred
by the Applicant for his impleadment in Company Petition (AT) (Ins.) No.
1612 of 2026. In order to deal with the argument extended by the learned
counsel for the Applicant, we will have to read the provision of Part-XI in
itself. The form and the nature of the affidavit, as contemplated under Part-
XI of the Rules, prescribes that it has to be in accordance with Order XIX
Rule 3 of the CPC. The purport of Order XIX Rule 3, which finds place under
Rule 68 of the NCLAT Rules, provides as to what and how the contents of
the affidavit would be. That was only for the purposes of verification of fact
as a deponent and its knowledge, to the deponent, regards to the contents,
to make the contents of affidavit judicially acceptable, and attach
truthfulness to the contents of the affidavit and not only the format of it.
Meaning thereby that the allegation of fraud in the affidavit in itself only

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
13 of 34
becomes relevant when the contents of the supporting affidavit are also
argued to be based upon fraud and falsity.
Order 19 Rule 3: -
“3. Matters to which affidavits shall be confined. —
(1) Affidavits shall be confined to such facts as the
deponent is able of his own knowledge to prove,
except on interlocutory applications, on which
statements of his belief may be admitted: provided
that the grounds thereof are stated.
(2) The costs of every affidavit which shall
unnecessarily set forth matters of hearsay or
argumentative matter, or copies of or extracts from
documents, shall (unless the Court otherwise directs)
be paid by the party filing the same.”

22.
According to Order XIX Rule 3, as made applicable by Rule 68 of the
NCLAT Rules, its only to attach fairness to the knowledge of the contents,
which has to be proved to be made acceptable in judicial proceedings by
affidavit, and when, in the instant case, the contents of the reply itself are
not denied by the Applicant Mr. Haravtar Singh Arora, the affidavit filed in
support thereto would be treated to be a rectifiable defect and it would not
malign the entire proceeding which already stands decided on merits, which
could sustain or permit the recall application preferred by the Appellant
seeking recall of the Order dated 10.09.2026, which in itself was a contested
and concluded proceedings on merits.

23.
Reverting back to the contents of Part-XI of the NCLAT Rules, Rule 72,
if it exclusively pertains to “verification of a document” accompanying an

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
14 of 34
affidavit, for which an attestor has to make an endorsement that the
documents marked in Annexures are true in their contents. Rule 72 in itself
only speaks about an “attestation”, which was a requirement under law,
which, in the instant case, stood satisfied by the affidavit of 02.09.2026.
Hence, the condition of attestation made by the Notary in the affidavit of
02.09.2026, as provided under Rule 72 of the NCLAT Rules, was satisfied.

24.
Even in accordance with prescription of the format, prescribed for the
affidavits as per the NCLAT Rules, as contemplated under Rule 68, it
provides hereunder: -
“Form NCLAT-4
[See Rule 68]
IN THE NATIONAL COMPANY LAW APPELLATE TRIBUNAL
______________BENCH
Appeal/Petition/ /No. of 20_________
Appellant/Applicant
vs
Respondent/s
AFFIDAVIT
I, .................................. aged...................... years,
son/daughter/wife
of
............
..........................(name
and
occupation
of
the
deponent)..................................... residing at (Full
address) ........................................do hereby swear
in the name of God/solemnly affirm and state as
follows:

Para. 1
Para. 2
Para. 3
......................................
Contents of Paragraphs Nos. ......................are within
my personal knowledge and contents of Paragraphs
Nos...............are based on information received by
me which I believe the same to be true (state the
source of information wherever possible and the
grounds for belief, if any ).
Place :

Signature of the Deponent

Date :

Name in Block Letters

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
15 of 34
No. of corrections on page nos.

Identified by:

Before me
*.............................................................................

Sworn/solemnly affirmed before me on this the
.......................day of ...200.............

Signature
(Name and Designation of
the Attesting Authority with Seal)

*To add endorsement in Form No. when necessary”

25.
This format of the affidavit too, if it is read in consonance with Part-XI,
Form NCLAT-4, issued under Rule 68, prescribes the format of the affidavit,
which has been given hereinabove. The counsel for the Applicant has argued
there was no “swearing” in the affidavit filed with the reply by the Appellant
in opposition to the Impleadment Application No. 6230 of 2026. This
argument is not acceptable, also for the reason that, according to the format
of the affidavit given above, under NCLAT Form-4, it does not speak about
swearing of an affidavit; it only speaks about attestation of the affidavit. In
that eventuality too, the affidavit filed by the Appellant in reply to the
impleadment application cannot be falsified to be actuated by fraud to
deceive in any manner whatsoever.

26.
A provision of law has to be pragmatically read in its totality to lead to
its logical objective. The authority of authorization given to a person under
Rule 69 of the NCLAT Rules, 2016 gives an option that the affidavit shall be
“sworn or affirmed” before an officer or a Notary Public. Since the present
affidavit dated 02.09.2026 was an affidavit attested by the Notary, as
permitted under Rule 69 of the NCLAT Rules, 2016 it cannot be said that

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
16 of 34
the affidavit dated 02.09.2026 was a fraudulent document or that it was
vitiated by its contents too, in the light of the provisions contained under
Order XIX Rule 3 of the CPC, as attracted by Rule 68 of the NCLAT Rules.

27.
Even in the absence of swearing (though not specifically required), the
attestation exclusively in itself could still be permissible to read the affidavit
in support of an application, which, in the instant case, was an accepted
document by the Applicant to the recall application having contested upon it
on merits. More glaringly, when the purpose of the affidavit, as per the
language of Part-XI of the NCLAT Rules, 2016 is to provide authenticity to
the affidavit and its contents, when the contents themselves are not denied
by the Applicant even today in an application for recall preferred even today,
the affidavit filed in support thereto cannot itself be rendered to be bad in
the eyes of law because no element of fraud exists so far as the necessity of
swearing of contents of affidavit, as argued by the learned counsel for the
Applicant, is concerned.

28.
The argument advanced by the learned counsel for the Applicant
regarding the necessity of swearing is not acceptable, once again for the
reason that, according to Rules 69 and 70 of NCLAT Rules, 2016 it provides
that an affidavit has to be “sworn or affirmed”, which means that it could be
either way. The affidavit could be taken and considered in the proceedings,
whether it is sworn or affirmed. Here, the use of the word “or” in between
the expressions given in Rules 69 and 70 is not to be read as the word
“and”. Hence, either swearing of an affidavit or attestation of an affidavit in

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
17 of 34
accordance with Part-XI of the Rules would still be an acceptable attestation
for reading a document for the purposes of the proceedings.

29.
The reference made to Rule 72 by the learned counsel for the
Applicant is absolutely untenable because there is no fraud as such, and
the same cannot be accepted by this Tribunal while exercising our powers
for consideration of recall application, seeking recall of the Order, which is
restricted to the Order in itself, and more particularly when the contents of
the reply and the supporting affidavit are not denied by the Applicant’s
counsel.

30.
As we have already observed, the Appellant before this Tribunal, who
is an RP, was as against the Order of suspension of the licence for a period
of one year in pursuance of the action taken against him by the Disciplinary
Committee. The Applicant, in the capacity of being the shareholder, Director
or promoter of a third entity, not party to the proceedings, cannot be said to
be at all necessary party in the absence of whom the disciplinary
proceedings against the Appellant could not be decided because the
Applicants claim would not be falling under or within the ambit of Order I
Rule 8A of the CPC, as prayed for by the Applicant.

31.
As we have already observed, the principal proceedings as against the
Appellant had been in the shape of disciplinary proceedings drawn against
him in accordance with Regulation 13 of the IBBI (Inspection and
Investigation) Regulations, 2017. It was altogether a different subject that

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
18 of 34
was under consideration in the Company Appeal. Which had no nexus to
the stand taken by the Applicant in his impleadment application.

32.
The application for intervention/impleadment, though it was bad in
law because it was not supported with the valid Power of Attorney, as
mentioned in the note clause of the application, which was not supplied
even till the date when the Order was passed, was also not maintainable on
the said ground.

33.
Besides that, since the intervention was being sought by the Applicant
because of the fact that it impacts upon the liquidation proceedings drawn
as against M/s James Hotel Limited, of which the Applicant claims himself
to be the Director, Promoter, shareholder, and which has already been
placed under liquidation in a pending proceeding, CP (IB) No. 15 of 2026,
Punjab National Bank versus James Hotel, in which the present Appellant
has been appointed as a liquidator, it is contended by the Appellant that his
rights would also be affected because of the impugned Order, which is the
subject matter of challenge in the instant Company Appeal.

34.
It is argued by the learned counsel for the Appellant that, because of
the observations made in Para 3.3 of the impugned Order, since there
happens to be a suspension of the Appellant from carrying out any
liquidation proceedings in relation to other entities, it may affect the
proceedings of the liquidation of M/s James Hotel Limited. For that purpose,
Para 3.3 of the impugned Order has to be read together with the first part of
Para 3.3.

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
19 of 34

35.
The copy of the Order suspending the licence of the IRP for a period of
two years under Section 220 of the Code, to be read with Regulation 13,
does not at all affect any right of the Applicant for the reason being that the
direction contained in the second part of Para 3.3 of the Order was that the
CoC of the respective CDs shall replace Mr. Navneet Gupta with another
Resolution Professional in accordance with Section 27 of the Code.

36.
The Applicant is not a member of the CoC for whom the direction was
issued as per Para 3.3 of the impugned Order for replacing the Resolution
Professional. As such, since the Appellant is not part of the CoC to whom
the direction has been issued for removal of the Resolution Professional, the
Applicant does not become a necessary party at all to be impleaded what to
say about recall of Order rejecting his impleadment. Thus, it has been
rightly observed in the Order dated 10.09.2026, the Applicant would not be
necessary party whose presence would be at all needed to decide the
Company Appeal.

37.
Because of the fact that there is no fraud which is apparently
established, merely because of the execution of the affidavit, the same is not
accepted by this Tribunal. Thus the recall though not permissible cannot be
permitted to be ventured on its merits and deserves rejection.

38.
The argument in the context of Para 3.3, as raised by the Appellant,
that it concerns him also is absolutely unfounded, because it was a general
direction that was issued for a restraint as against the Appellant from

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
20 of 34
carrying out any proceedings as an Resolution Professional. However, that is
to be exercised subject to certain riders, where the CoC of the respective
CDs were supposed to restrain the Appellant from functioning as an IRP or a
Resolution Professional in the light of the provisions contained under
Section 27 of the Code.

39.
This direction given in Para 3.3 was not unfettered, as it was not
specifically confined to the Applicant; rather, it was restricted for complying
with the provisions contained under Section 27 of the Code. Hence, this in
itself too, will not entitle the Applicant to be impleaded, as argued by the
counsel for the Applicant, that he becomes a necessary party, to the
proceedings of this Company Appeal.

40.
The rejection of his impleadment by an Order dated 10.09.2026 is
backed by the fact that no aspect of fraud is made out by the Applicant as
against the Order dated 10.09.2026, particularly in relation to the reply
submitted by the Appellant to the impleadment application. The plea of
fraud fails, more particularly when the plea of fraud attempts to enter de
novo into the merits of the decision taken on merits, i.e., the Order dated
10.09.2026. The same cannot be exercised when fraud itself is not
established.

41.
The learned counsel for the Applicant to the recall application has
primarily concentrated his argument from two perspectives, the one which
we have already dealt with hereinabove, with regards the aspect of fraud. To
attract those principles of fraud, it is necessary that the act complained of

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
21 of 34
must satisfy the ingredients required to establish fraud. Merely a projected
plea by the counsel for the Applicant alleging bald allegation of fraud,
cannot, in itself, lead to a conclusion that it is a fraud effecting merits, and
more particularly when it is being generated by professional acumen of the
counsel, in order to sustain the application for recall, which otherwise is not
permissible under law, so far as it relates to the proceedings under the IBC,
where a recall cannot be camouflaged to be adopted as a recourse of review.

42.
For filing a recall on the basis of fraud, it is necessary for the
Applicant to establish the parameters required to be satisfied to conclude
that it is a fraud on fact effecting decision. Fraud, in its normal connotation,
is a wrongful and criminal deception. It is intended to result in financial or
personal gain. In the instant case, none of the ingredients was intended to
be attain either a financial or personal gain by the Appellant herein, in
whose favour the Order has been passed on an intervention application
preferred by the Applicant, are established.
43.
The prime object for fraud is that it has to have an intention,
“intention to deceive”, by unjustifiably claiming or being credited with
accomplishment or qualities of gain. As we have already discussed above,
the pleadings raised in the recall application do not satisfy the aspect of
fraud merely on the ground of the clauses contained in the affidavit and the
way it has been interpreted by the learned counsel for the Applicant, when
he had failed to establish, as to what was the intent to illegally gain the
benefit, so far as it related to pressing of the application for intervention.

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
22 of 34
44.
Literally, the fraud, as per the Oxford Dictionary, reads as under:-
“wrongful or criminal deception intended to result in
financial or personal gain: he was convicted of fraud
prosecutions for social security frauds. Person or thing
intended to deceive others, typically by unjustifiably
claiming or being credited with accomplishments or
qualities: mediums exposed as tricksters and frauds.
- ORIGIN MIDDLE ENGLISH: from Old French fraude,
from Latin fraud, fraud-‘deceit, injury”

45.
Even according to the Law Lexicon, it deals with as to what actually
the term “fraud” means under law, and it has widely described it that it
means that it should aim to deceive in the grant of a benefit in a proceeding
or while dealing with any other aspect which monetarily benefits the person
who exercises fraud. It cannot be utilized as a general expression for the
purposes of every misrepresentation or a concealment, which can constitute
misrepresentation but not fraud.

46.
The Webster’s Third New International Dictionary has defined “fraud”
in the following terms: “It is an act or an omission to act or concealment by
which one person obtains an advantage against conscious over another or
which equity or public policy forbids as being prejudicial to another.”

47.
None of these principles would be attracted in the present case, where
the fact of establishment of fraud itself is not made out because of the
reasons which we have already considered above.

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
23 of 34
48.
The explanation given therein of fraud in the Oxford Dictionary, if it is
read in the context of criminal law, which deals with its finalization upon
holding of an offence of fraud, is dealt with under the Indian Penal Code
(IPC) under Section 415, which is a criminal Act and which has certain
background, which is otherwise motivated by an act of deceiving or
dishonestly inducing a person to believe something which is not otherwise
true. The element of fraud as contemplated under Section 415 of the IPC, to
be read with Section 318 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which
requires a satisfaction before a criminal prosecution is required to be carried
for the offence of fraud. Even as per the expression given by the statute
under Section 415 of the IPC and Section 318 of the BNS, the entire
allegation raised by the Applicant to the recall application does not lead to
draw an impeccable inference that the Appellant can at all be saddled with
the responsibility of having an intention to cheat or dishonestly inducing to
gain a right, and that too, as we have already observed above, the Applicant
had been contesting the proceedings before this Tribunal.

49.
He had with all sincerity, and overwhelming diligence, had
participated in the proceedings while pressing upon his application, which
has been decided on merits by the Order dated 10.09.2026, rejecting his
impleadment application being I.A. No. 6230 of 2026. When this Tribunal
had voluntarily completed the proceedings and the same stood rejected
based upon the affidavit filed by the Appellant, the Applicant now cannot, at
a subsequent stage, take a malicious somersault and fish out the ground of
fraud, which otherwise was also available to him to be pressed at the time

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
24 of 34
when the application I.A. No. 6230 of 2026 was being considered by this
Tribunal and was being pressed on merits. Having not done so, it is no more
open for the Appellant to argue that the reply filed by the Appellant in
response to I.A. No. 6230 of 2026 was actuated by fraud, so as to enable
him to sustain his recall application, to have a new enmity to press his
application under Order I Rule 8A of CPC, preferred in the shape of
impleadment, and that in an Appeal by Appellant against disciplinary
proceedings.

50.
Because of the fact that the parameters those were required to be
satisfied for completing and complaining an act of fraud have not been
satisfied, owing to the grounds taken by the Applicant, the plea is not
acceptable by us. In the absence of the same, the application for recall,
which in fact is being camouflaged as seeking a review, which is not
otherwise permissible under law, would not be maintainable and, hence,
would deserve rejection.

51.
Learned counsel for the Applicant to the recall application has raised
a peculiar argument and, it would not be out of context to submit, an
irrational ground too. That the conduct of the counsel for Appellant itself
was bad and he ought to have taken care of the earlier Order passed by the
Tribunal in some other matter, where the counsel was granted an
opportunity to rectify the defects in the affidavit. In relation thereto, while
elaborating his argument, the learned counsel, particularly while remarking
upon the conduct of the counsel for the Appellant in person as an

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
25 of 34
individual, who has filed the reply in opposition to the intervention
application, has extracted some Order passed in some other Comp. App.
(AT) No. 43 of 2026, as against the counsel, on that basis observing thereof
that the Appellant was conscious of the fact that the affidavits would be
rectifiable defects and thus, in that eventuality, he made reference to the
Order dated 17.02.2026 as passed in Comp. App. (AT) No. 43 of 2026, which
has no nexus to the present proceedings of the intervention or the recall
application.

52.
Recall applicant argues, if that be a rectifiable defect, then the counsel
ought to have rectified it himself after seeking an opportunity from the
Tribunal. We make it very clear that the Order dated 17.02.2026 is not a
precedent or a ratio decidendi because that was an Order, which was passed
at an interlocutory stage in Comp. App. (AT) No. 43 of 2026, which was
altogether an independent proceeding having no relation to the present
Appeal. Since it is not a ratio decided, it cannot be taken as an authority,
that the counsel for the Appellant who had filed the reply, was conscious of
the fact of the probable expected rectification of defects, which he ought to
have carried. The gravamen of argument is more of personnel against
counsel, rather than the case itself.

53.
This stand taken, though it may be professionally laudable, being
against the fraternity and for no good cause, is not acceptable by us and
stands turned down.

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
26 of 34
54.
The learned counsel for the Applicant has heavily relied upon the
written submissions and the Orders as filed in support thereto. Outrightly,
we decline to accept the same because the title head of the said written
submissions is in relation to I.A. No. 6680 of 2026, that has been preferred
in I.A. No. 6168 of 2026. This written submission is not in relation to I.A.
No. 6679 of 2026 filed by the Applicant, by virtue of which he has sought
the recall of the Order dated 10.09.2026. In that eventuality, the written
submissions in itself cannot be borrowed to be accepted or supplied while
deciding I.A. No. 6679 of 2026, when it has not been filed to be read in
relation to I.A. No. 6679 of 2026, which obviously has to be decided
independently, since filed by different applicant for different relief.

55.
What is important is that the application for recall was preferred by
the Applicant before the Registry on 14.09.2026. The proceedings were
taken up on 14.09.2026, whereby the Applicant’s counsel intimated about
filing of the application for recall, being I.A. No. 6679 of 2026, to which this
Tribunal directed the Registry to take note of it and to place the application
on the next date fixed, i.e., 16.09.2026.

56.
When the proceedings were taken up on 16.09.2026, the matter could
not be taken up. The counsel for the Applicant, Mr. Deepak Khosla, could
not participate in the proceedings because of his personal inconvenience
due to the ailment of his father, who was admitted in hospital. The said
request was opposed, as it was argued by the learned counsel for the
Appellant that it was a craft adopted by recall applicant’s counsel to adjourn

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
27 of 34
the proceedings and get it delayed. But still, this Tribunal accommodated
the Applicant’s counsel, Mr. Deepak Khosla, and placed the matter for
17.09.2026.

57.
On 17.09.2026, when the matter was taken up, it could be seen from
the proceedings as recorded, that the Tribunal, for the reasons recorded in
the Order dated 17.09.2026, had released the matter to be placed before
another Bench because at the stage of recall application, unnecessary
valuable time of the court was being consumed at the cost of the matter
listed on that date, owing to which the Hon’ble Acting Chairperson has
nominated this Bench.

58.
Why reference of these dates of 14.09.2026, 16.09.2026 and
17.09.2026 is required to be referred herein is because, on all these dates,
the application for recall, i.e., I.A. No. 6679 of 2026, filed by the
Respondent/Applicant through his counsel, Mr. Deepak Khosla, was never
addressed on merits.

59.
The proceedings of the application, upon the matter being posted
before us, were taken up on 21.09.2026. On 21.09.2026 itself, the
Applicant, through his counsel, Mr. Deepak Khosla, without a prior leave of
the Tribunal filed the written submissions. Filing of written submissions is
not customary, and filing of it does not depend upon the whims and fancies
of the party to the proceedings to file the written submissions as per their
choice. Filing of written submissions is only when the Court or the Tribunal
feels upon conclusion of arguments that its necessary and then when it

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
28 of 34
directs the party to file written submissions, it could be filed. Filing of a
written submission has to be with the prior leave of Tribunal, when the
Tribunal feels its necessary to facilitate and make the judgment dictation
convenient. Because by the time matter is argued counsel has sufficient
opportunity to raise all his pleadings.

60.
For that purpose, the principles have been enunciated under Order
XVIII Rule 3C and 3D of the CPC, which would be applicable, and it is not
as a matter of choice of the litigant or his counsel to file written submissions
without arguing the matter on merits and even being called by the Court,
because written submissions only facilitate the Tribunal when the Tribunal
or the Court feels that they are required to be filed.

61.
Though we have considered the written submissions as filed by the
Applicant’s counsel, on 21.09.2026, which contained pleading and material
even much beyond the recall application itself, which in impermissible to be
introduced at the stage of filing of written submission. When the application
itself was taken up on merits, under law, it was not required to be heard on
the basis of written submissions which was attempted by the learned
counsel, and that too particularly when it was introducing all the new facts
which were not even part and parcel when the arguments were extended in
the intervention application while passing of an Order dated 10.09.2026, or
even in the recall application.

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
29 of 34
62.
Thus, the plea of the written submissions is declined to be considered,
and more particularly when it is actuated by malice, intending to delay the
proceedings, and a consequence of professional acumen.

63.
In response, the learned counsel for the Appellant contended that all
these arguments are not open to be extended by the learned counsel for the
Applicant to the recall application, as the authority under which the
proceedings were taken i.e., Power of Attorney by the Applicant was not
placed on record despite the note clause as submitted in the application for
impleadment, i.e., I.A. No. 6230 of 2026, because till the arguments were
concluded on 10.09.2026, the Applicant didn’t had a valid attorney with the
deponent of the affidavit to the impleadment application, I.A. No. 6230 of
2026. Hence, it was a fallacious proceeding and it could not be considered.

64.
Though at this stage we are not required to venture into that issue,
though it may be having a bearing upon the sustainability of I.A. No. 6230 of
2026, we are refraining from making any observations because I.A. No. 6230
of 2026 seeking an intervention has already been decided on merits and, at
present, we are only seized with the recall application seeking recall of the
Order dated 10.09.2026.

65.
If we could summarise the manner in which the proceedings have
been taken for the recall application at the behest of the Applicant, through
his counsel, Mr. Deepak Khosla, it is a motivated proceeding catalyzed in
the shape of seeking a recall of an Order which has been otherwise passed
on merits on 10.09.2026, rejecting the Impleadment Application i.e., I.A. No.

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
30 of 34
6230 of 2026. It cannot be permitted to be revisited on the basis or under
the garb of the recall application, which is otherwise in the shape of a review
of the Order dated 10.09.2026 and is outside the scope of the procedures
contemplated under the IBC.

66.
Hence, the recall is misconceived and the same is accordingly rejected
with a cost of Rs. 5 Lakhs.

I.A. No. 6680 of 2026 (by Applicant Ajmair Singh Bhullar)
1.
This application is nothing but a consequence of a hardcore
conspiracy. The Applicant to I.A. No. 6680 of 2026, along with the Applicant
to I.A. No. 6679 of 2026 (Mr. Haravtar Singh Arora), both the Applicants,
have somehow conspired to ensure stall the proceedings of the instant
Company Appeal and, hence, by one way or another, they wanted to
interfere with the proceedings.

2.
Earlier, the Applicant, Mr. Haravtar Singh Arora’s application for
impleadment, already stood rejected by an Order dated 10.09.2026, which
has been sought to be recalled by him by filing recall application, being I.A.
No. 6679 of 2026, which we have rejected by this Order, for the reasons

3.
The Company Appeal is against an Order dated 21.08.2026 disposing
of the show-cause notice issued against the Appellant, Mr. Navneet Gupta,
the Insolvency Professional, for drawing the proceedings against him, for his
professional misconduct, as per the IBBI Regulations in these eventuality,

I.A. Nos. 6679 & 6680 of 2026 in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026
31 of 34
so far as the Applicant, Mr. Ajmair Singh Bhullar, is concerned, he, in any
capacity, has got nothing to do with the controversy involved in the
Company Appeal. Mr. Ajmair Singh Bhullar is not a party to the
proceedings, which are the subject matter of challenge in the Company
Appeal (AT) (Ins.) No. 1612 of 2026, nor has he been chosen by the
Appellant to be made as a party in the instant Company Appeal. As relief
sought in the Appeal relates or effects any of the legally sustainable rights of
the Applicants of both the applications.

4.

himself, to be made a party in a proceeding in which he is neither directly

Before us, under consideration are the two interlocutory applications,

While Mr. Ajmair Singh Bhullar, sought his limited impleadment in stay

It becomes indispensable for us to directly consider the application
bearing I.A. No. 6679 of 2026, itself without considering the background and
the manner in which the proceedings have been traversed by the Applicant.

The Company Appeal had been preferred by Mr. Navneet Gupta, the
Insolvency Resolution Professional, wherein the IBBI, the Regulator while
considering the response of Appellant, as submitted in response to the Show

has been impugned by the Appellant:

3.2. This Order shall come into force on expiry of 30

4.
Consequent to the establishment of set of allegations relating to
proportional misconduct the Resolution Professional and the observations
which have been made by the Disciplinary Committee, in exercise of its
statutory powers conferred to it under Section 220 of the Code, which is to
be read with Regulation 13 of the IBBI (Inspection and Investigation)
Regulations, 2017, suspended the registration of Mr. Navneet Gupta, the
IRP (Appellant), for a period of one year.

5.
The Order, in itself, has been directed to be made effective after the
expiry of 30 days from the date of its issuance. What would be more
concerning would be the observations made in Para No. 3.3 of the impugned
Order, which has been argued by the counsel for the parties, whereby the
